subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat render identity avatars directly from remote URLs, and if so, which URL schemes and network destinations are acceptable?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes the desktop webview from local/data image sources to arbitrary network image sources; that product and security boundary cannot be selected safely by an automated repair.

options.title: Keep local and data-backed avatars only
options.body: Retain the existing local/data image CSP and normalize supported workspace avatars to bounded data URIs before rendering.

options.title: Permit HTTPS avatars with an explicit policy
options.body: Allow only HTTPS remote avatars after documenting the network/privacy trade-off and adding focused validation and runtime proof.

options.title: Approve HTTP and HTTPS avatars
options.body: Accept the broad remote-image behavior as a supported Linux Quick Chat capability and document the resulting network-fetch policy.

recommendation.title: Keep local and data-backed avatars only
recommendation.body: Retain the existing local/data image CSP and normalize supported workspace avatars to bounded data URIs before rendering.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and current branch place this person closest to the Quick Chat implementation, although the final trust-policy choice remains a maintainer decision.
